stem: In a prone position, what motor milestone is typically expected of a healthy $6$-month-old infant?

options.text: Lifting the head for only a few seconds
Chest coming off the ground with elbows bent
Chest fully up with arms extended and head vertical
Rolling from back to front only

explanation: By $6$ months, infants should have the strength to fully extend their arms and maintain a vertical head position while prone.
rationale: Focus on the progression of arm extension and head verticality as the infant grows stronger.

optionExplanations.A: This level of head control is generally expected earlier, around $6$ weeks of age.
optionExplanations.B: This posture is more characteristic of a $3$-month-old infant rather than a $6$-month-old.
optionExplanations.C: By $6$ months, infants should have the strength to fully extend their arms and maintain a vertical head position while prone.
optionExplanations.D: While rolling is a milestone, the specific prone position assessment focuses on weight-bearing and head control verticality.

source.hint: Focus on the progression of arm extension and head verticality as the infant grows stronger.
